chain.label: Older-design 0.38-inch-radius midspar fitting susceptible to fatigue cracking
chain.trigger: The plated radii in the No. 2 pylon midspar fittings were measured at a nominal 0.38 inch, identifying them as the older style fittings that should have been replaced in accordance with the effective AD.

chain.label: Previous owner erroneously recorded the repetitive midspar AD as complete in 1983
chain.trigger: in 1983, a previous owner/operator had marked the compliance status of the AD in effect at the time (77-09-03) with 'C' (meaning complete)... the compliance status for the AD should have been recorded as 'REP' for repetitive.

chain.label: No requirement for an acquiring operator to physically verify recorded AD compliance
chain.trigger: Federal regulations do not require an owner/operator acquiring an aircraft to physically verify the compliance of every AD for which compliance has been recorded.

chain.label: Undetected critical fatigue crack in No. 2 pylon inboard midspar fitting; old fittings never replaced and inspections deleted in 2003
chain.trigger: The No. 2 engine pylon midspar fitting had a preexisting fatigue crack that had propagated to a critical length before or during the accident flight takeoff... Omega deleted the inspection requirement from its maintenance plan.

caused_by.evidence: an older fitting design... calling for repetitive visual inspections and eventual replacement with a more fatigue-resistant design incorporating a 1.0-inch radius

This status reconfirmed to Omega that the records showed the fittings had been replaced and inspections were no longer necessary, and Omega deleted the inspection requirement from its maintenance plan.
there were no additional or different civil airworthiness or operating requirements that would have led to a specific inspection of the fittings to verify compliance with the AD

chain.label: No. 2 midspar fitting fractured and the pylon with engine separated from the left wing just after liftoff
chain.trigger: On the takeoff roll, shortly after liftoff, the No. 2 engine pylon separated from the left wing.

caused_by.evidence: the upper and lower tangs of the inboard midspar fitting on the No 2. pylon, which failed due to fatigue

chain.label: Loss of thrust from both left engines after the departing No. 2 nacelle struck the No. 1 nacelle
chain.trigger: The No. 2 engine nacelle and pylon assembly struck the No. 1 engine nacelle, causing the No. 1 engine inlet cowl to separate, which degraded the engine's ability to produce thrust and resulted in a significant loss of thrust on the left side of the airplane.

caused_by.evidence: the No. 2 (left inboard) engine separated and traveled up above the left wing... The inlet cowling for the No. 1 (left outboard) engine separated immediately thereafter, consistent with being struck by the No. 2 engine nacelle.

chain.label: Right crosswind 24 knots gusting to 34 knots on runway 21
chain.trigger: the reported wind was from 280º magnetic at 24 knots, gusting to 34 knots

chain.label: Airplane could not climb and began descending while drifting left despite full right rudder and aileron
chain.trigger: he applied full right rudder and near full right aileron to maintain directional control and level the wings, but the airplane continued to drift to the left... The airplane began to descend with the remaining three engine power levers at maximum power

caused_by.evidence: The loss of thrust from both left engines made it highly unlikely that the airplane would be able to continue with a successful takeoff
he applied forward pressure on the yoke and right aileron input to compensate for the right crosswind

chain.label: Captain rejected the takeoff and put the airplane back down on the remaining runway
chain.trigger: The captain decided to reject the takeoff and attempt to land on the remaining runway... the pilot's decision to reject the takeoff was appropriate and properly executed.

caused_by.evidence: The captain reported that he perceived the airplane would not continue to climb and decided to 'put it back on the ground.'
considering the possibility of serious structural damage, the pilot's decision to reject the takeoff was appropriate

chain.label: Airplane bounced, drifted left and departed the runway surface near taxiway A1
chain.trigger: The airplane made multiple contacts with the runway before drifting left and departing the runway surface before the airplane reached taxiway A1.

caused_by.evidence: he lowered the nose and leveled the wings just as the airplane touched down on the runway between taxiway A2 and A1
the left wing dipped slightly... loss of the inlet cowling on the No. 1 engine would increase drag, effectively resulting in less than zero thrust output
departed the runway on a 218º heading near taxiway A1

chain.label: Airplane crossed taxiway A, came to rest in a marsh and was substantially damaged by postimpact fire
chain.trigger: The airplane collided with a marsh area to the left side beyond the departure end of the runway and was substantially damaged by postimpact fire.

caused_by.evidence: continued across the grass infield and taxiway A before coming to rest in a saltwater marsh where it caught fire

chain.label: Three flight crewmembers sustained minor injuries
chain.trigger: The three flight crewmembers sustained minor injuries.

caused_by.evidence: The flight crew observed flames in the cabin area... All three crewmembers successfully evacuated through the left forward entrance via the escape slide.
